html:
SMTO-GWT-0001 — Agent unavailable

GUID: 59a7cbe0-24f6-457e-9195-560c8243ee81
Slug: agent-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach the computer you picked to do this work, so your new request didn't start. Work sent to that computer in earlier tasks may still have run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and find the Gateway you chose for this task. If its Enabled switch is Off, turn it On. A Gateway that is switched off can't receive new tasks, so SMTO stops the request before it starts.
  2. Make sure the computer running that Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands there) is switched on and online, then select Check connection on its row. If the status reads Connection failed, SMTO can't reach that computer at all.
  3. If the row shows the wrong address, select Edit, correct Host and Port, and select Save changes. A missing or outdated address leaves SMTO with nowhere to send the work.
  4. Before you resend, look at the earlier tasks in this conversation to see whether their work on that computer already finished. Losing the connection doesn't undo work that was already sent, and repeating it could do it twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's row shows Connected, and when you send the request the task starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer or installed SMTO. Don't resend earlier work until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Request submission stopped at the availability check because the selected Gateway is disabled, not configured, or did not answer its connection check.

What this means

  • The runtime could not communicate with the selected Gateway. It may be offline, disabled, misconfigured or unreachable from the runtime; the current connection state distinguishes these possibilities. This availability error does not settle the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The selected Gateway has no usable connection from the runtime. Service state, selection and network reachability require separate checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected Gateway and its connection status in Mission Control. Ask its operator to confirm the service is running on the expected endpoint; for prior dispatched work, inspect the saved receipt and current state.

How to fix it

  • Read the availability status (disabled, unconfigured or offline) and last_error in Technical details. Enable the Gateway record, or correct its host/port (or gateway_url / gateway_endpoints for the default Gateway), and confirm a passing health check; before resubmitting, confirm the outcome of any previously dispatched operation from its saved receipt.
  • Check the selected Gateway’s connection status and configured endpoint in Mission Control. Restore the connection, then reconcile any previously dispatched operation before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway reports its identity and supported capabilities; outstanding work has a known receipt or remains explicitly unresolved.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Availability or connection failure does not establish nonexecution for a previously dispatched operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
